Hi Alex — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and next steps so we have alignment on the PoC scope and SLOs. Please chime in if I missed anything.

Call highlights (from our side):
- PoC goal: validate low-latency streaming for realtime payment authorization UX and measure unit cost at expected peak load.
- Target latency: p95 <= 200ms for single-turn streaming responses (up to 512 tokens).
- Throughput/Concurrency: baseline expected steady concurrent requests = 200 parallel active streams; peak burst to ~500 for short windows (1–3 minutes) during batch jobs and peak hours.
- Connection model: long-lived websockets preferred; client re-use of a connection with multiplexed streams is ideal. If using HTTP/2 keep-alive, we expect 6–8 concurrent requests per connection.
- Rate limits: we discussed a per-account token cap and a per-connection QPS limit; you asked for flexibility during peak windows and a buffer for retries.

Action items / next steps:
1) I’ll return a short technical spec listing connection-pool recommendations and a suggested quota profile for your expected load — will attach.
2) Please confirm whether your clients will use websockets or HTTP/2 (we need this to recommend pool sizing).
3) If procurement needs official numbers for pricing, loop them in and we’ll provide a PoC quote + temporary increased quota.

Attachments: I’ll follow up with a connection-specs spreadsheet and a draft SLA.

Thanks — Grace

Alex — thanks. Attached is the connection-pool spreadsheet I promised (conn_specs.xlsx). Key recommendations from the engineering side: 

- Pool sizing (websockets): allocate dedicated connection pool of 1 connection per ~6 clients for muxed streams (i.e., ~200 active streams = ~34 connections). Recommend a reserved pool of 40 connections for steady-state and burst headroom.
- Parallel streams per connection: assume safe multiplexing of up to 16 logical streams per socket for our runtime; set conservative default at 8 for the PoC.
- Per-connection QPS: recommend a soft cap of 120 QPS per connection to avoid head-of-line issues; total account-level QPS should be set to accommodate steady + burst.
- Concurrency quota: suggest reserved concurrency = 250 parallel logical streams, with a burst policy up to 500 for up to 2 minutes. Redwood can enforce a sliding-window burst allowance and fall back to a queued model (retry w/ backoff) if capacity is exceeded.
- Streaming SLO: p95 latency target = 200ms; we can accept up to 220ms temporarily during cold-cache startup or heavy KV cache misses.
- Fallback behavior: when quota exceeded, Redwood will return 429 with Retry-After headers for synchronous calls and for streaming attempt graceful termination with a short retry token; recommend client-side exponential backoff starting at 200ms.

Please review the attached sheet — the tab "PoC-profile" summarizes the numbers I listed. If that looks good, I’ll propose a temporary quota profile and a priced PoC in a follow-up.

Thanks — Grace
